newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB to move bond dealing team from Goodbody.
newsitem.headline: AIB to move bond dealing team from Goodbody.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks is planning to move its bond dealing team from Goodbody Stockbrokers and merge it with its AIB Capital Markets operation in Dublin's IFSC, banking sources confirmed on Wednesday.
Just 10 staff out of 140 would be affected by the move which would leave Goodbody to concentrate on equity dealing, corporate finance and private clients, the sources said.
"It's not a great, big restructure of Goodbodys," one source told Reuters.

Goodbody is one of six market-makers in Irish government bonds and AIB Capital Markets would have to apply for membership of the Irish Stock Exchange as a primary dealer to allow the transfer of the bond desk to go ahead.
It would also need clearance from the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) which oversees the market-making system.
The move to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) is part of the reason behind the transfer of the bond desk, the sources said.
According to market sources, Goodbody ranks fourth in market share terms among the four Irish market-makers.
This, plus the desire to integrate all of AIB's Irish-pound market operations under one roof, were other reasons behind the proposal, media reports said.
